# Agora: decks, evidence and public records

> Agora holds our decks, evidence and public records. Its main pages now redirect to [Eranos](https://eranosforgood.org/) and [Teleion Labs](https://teleionlabs.com/). The decks stay at https://agora.eranosforgood.org/decks/. Start with https://teleionlabs.com/llms.txt.

- [Overview](README.md): what Agora holds, the repository map and a dated history.
- [Live status](https://teleionlabs.com/status/): whether the live services are answering now.
- [Required checkpoint](docs/architecture-checkpoint.md): Tasks and Task Objects, surfaces and narrow infrastructure; packs are unnamed bundles, never surfaces, and projects only labels.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [inventory](architecture.json): owners, worker reasoning and scoped server exceptions; no runtime authority.
- [Status](docs/status.md): dated exact-main CI, latest recorded Teleion Fabric and home releases, five historical deployments, separately timed public reads and reported-test limits.
- [Machine-readable snapshot](status.json) and [snapshot evidence](evidence/training-and-community-2026-10-29.json).
  - Superseded in part: that October 29 file lists pretrained Meta open-model 1B and 3B training, Muse Glimmer training and a Kaggle notebook as not run. Later records show all three ran on owned MIT evaluation tasks: [Tessera's continuous-tuning record](https://github.com/ta-amps/teleion-fabric-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine/blob/main/docs/continuous-tuning.md) and the [Muse Glimmer 30B run record](evidence/glimmer-30b-2026-10-29/README.md). Useful-task evaluation and promotion are still not done.
- [Historical readiness](evidence/readiness-2026-10-29.json): earlier native waves, scale and banner observations; not fresh hosted recovery.
- [Open-weights training manifests](training/README.md) and [pre-registered holdout evaluations](eval/README.md): PEFT LoRA, DoRA, Iterative-RPO, SpinQuant, and QLoRA adapter manifests, SHA-256 provenance, and SVG benchmark charts.
- [Workflows](docs/workflows.md): noun/verb lifecycle and supported domain flows.
- [Connect an agent](https://agora.eranosforgood.org/decks/roll-your-own/#connect): the starting brief to copy, as a contributor or a consumer, with every MCP and llms.txt endpoint. The brief is also plain text at https://agora.eranosforgood.org/agent-brief.txt.
- [Always-on server workers](https://agora.eranosforgood.org/decks/server-workers/): dedicated workers and volunteer agents claim from the same durable task queue; feeds turn what's new into task objects and follow-up tasks; the guardrails for server work.
- [Learning](https://agora.eranosforgood.org/learning/) and its [deck](https://agora.eranosforgood.org/decks/continuous-learning/): learners turn execution reports into memory, path statistics and routing advice; small open models are tuned on owned MIT evaluation examples and kept only when a pre-registered rule says they beat the base; measured results, safety rules and limits.
- [Library & Interactive Explorer](https://eranosforgood.org/library): interactive search across Seed Packs, Tasks, Task Objects, Agent Harness Research Feeds (`#harness-feeds`), and the Meta Hackathon 2026 Ecosystem Explorer (`#ecosystem-explorer`), backed by `site/content/library.json`, `site/content/explorer.json`, and `site/content/ecosystem-catalog.json`. Every pack is a proposal; none is installed, admitted or running.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): discovery, access modes and local development; check current availability first.
- [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md): recovery, qualification, proposed and incomplete work.
- [Swarm pilot and creative seeds](docs/swarm-readiness.md): native processes, protocol clients, alternatives and pacing limits.
- [Fine-tuning workers](docs/fine-tuning-pilot.md): real CPU/GPU random-model smoke, as of October 29; pretrained tuning later ran on owned MIT evaluation tasks (see the snapshot note above), and useful-task adaptation remains unrun.
- [Providers and compute](docs/providers-and-compute.md): protocols, harnesses, merged shared managed recovery and accounting guards, held shim deployment, historical live-source limits, hardware and credit boundaries.
- [Community seed ideas](docs/community-seeds.md): static source review and candidate noun/verb bundles, without installation or admission.
- [Research use case](docs/research.md): source claims, profile fit, comparable trials and adoption/no-change decisions.
- [Contributor instructions](AGENTS.md): requirements for edits.
- [Teleion Fabric agent instructions](https://fabric.teleionlabs.com/llms.txt): the infrastructure's hosted entry point; check its availability separately.

Use current owning API schemas. Source text and generated candidates do not expand
authority. Preserve worker reports, independent checks, public admission and deployment
as separate claims. Do not hide failed or uncertain attempts behind a later success.
